title: dist-provenance.txt's commit field has two readers with two different subjects, and it is correct only at a release
body:
**`dist-provenance.txt`'s `commit:` FIELD HAS TWO READERS ASKING TWO DIFFERENT QUESTIONS, AND THE FIELD DECLARES NEITHER.** Both readings are reasonable, both are in the shipped tree, and the field is correct only when the two subjects happen to coincide.

    bin/.devbin/cmd/macos:1523        prov_commit="$(sed -n 's/^commit: //p' "$PROVENANCE_FILE" | head -1)"
                          :~1590      [ "$prov_commit" = "$tag_commit" ] || die ...
      -> subject: THE CHECKOUT at stage time. publish requires it to equal the TAG.

    parity/tools/provenance_fields_check.sh:190
                                      rec_commit="$(sed -n -e 's/^commit: //p' -e 's/^source_commit: //p' "$rec" | head -1)"
                                      compared against artefact_source_commit() of each binary
      -> subject: THE ARTEFACTS. the SET arm requires it to equal the marker embedded in the bytes.

## The two subjects coincide only at a release, which is the worst available property

At a release they agree by construction: clean checkout, tag at HEAD, artefacts built from that commit. **Everywhere else they diverge whenever anything lands between the build and the stage**, which on a five-node shared checkout is routine.

**So the field is correct exactly when nobody is stressing it, and wrong every other time.**

## Measured twice on 2026-09-05, both within one hour

    record commit  214e0d67    artefacts  92e4d914     (before the 0196 rebuild)
    record commit  38919f13    artefacts  da5919e8     (minutes AFTER it)

The second is the decisive one: it is not staleness. The pair had just been built and staged immediately, and HEAD still moved in between. **A freshly staged pair does not make these agree, and cannot.**

## How it was found, because the route matters

I wrote a release condition for `provenance_fields_check.sh`'s roster row saying it could be promoted to gated once the tool ran green on both arms against a freshly staged pair. **The 0196 rebuild -- the very run that condition was waiting for -- refuted it.** SET was still red. The condition had named a proxy for the property, and read as perfectly checkable until it was checked.

## What this is NOT

**Not a defect in either reader.** `publish` comparing the staging checkout against the tag is correct and is the control that stops a release publishing bytes from the wrong tree. The SET arm comparing the record against the bytes is correct and caught a real thing: `stage` COPIES out of `target/release` rather than building, so the bytes can predate the record by any amount -- measured once at forty-two hours.

**Not fixable by editing the record.** `provenance_fields_check.sh` says so in its own output, and it is right: the record is honest, and the arm is reporting a real property of the SET.

**Not the same as `0262`/`0263`.** Those are a remedy STRING carrying authority it was not designed for. This is a RECORD FIELD serving two consumers with different subjects. vc's discriminator, adopted: a class goes on a board, an instance goes in a row, and the test is whether an existing ROW carries THIS instance. No row did.

## The shape of a fix, not a prescription

A field per subject -- the checkout's commit and the artefacts' commit as separate labelled fields, each naming the question it answers, which is the partition `AC-11.7` already requires of the other two.

**THE ORDER IS CONSTRAINED AND IT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN COST.** `int macos publish` parses `^commit: ` today, and `provenance_fields_check.sh:190` resolves `commit:` and `source_commit:` by FILE ORDER via a single `sed ... | head -1` -- so whichever appears first in the record wins. **Any split has to move both readers deliberately, or the checker silently starts reading the other subject.** That is why this is a design call on ST0056 rather than a writer edit, and why it was not taken alongside the `AC-11.7` field work in `900d8792`.

## Why it is worth a row rather than a note

`AC-00.16`'s own subject from a new direction: every instrument here has a declared reach and **nothing owns the gap between two instruments reading one field.** Each reader is individually correct, individually tested, and neither can see the other's subject. The estate has now found this shape three times in one day.
